description: Complete user journey maps for all 8 user types plus onboarding flows, conversion funnels, and retention hooks

user_types.label: Emerging Creator
user_types.description: Solo creator building an audience. Learning what works. Needs simplicity over power. Time-poor, tool-overwhelmed. Came from Linktree + Canva + multiple social apps and wants one place.
goals: Grow audience across platforms without managing each one individually
Monetize early with digital products or community access
Build a consistent posting cadence without burnout
Understand what content performs and double down
pain_points: Managing 4-6 social platforms manually is exhausting
No clear view of what is working across platforms
Revenue tools are fragmented — Gumroad for products, Patreon for subs, separate for courses
Cannot afford $200/month in stacked SaaS subscriptions
Posting is inconsistent because the workflow is too many steps

journey_stages.trigger: Sees creator they follow using CreatorOS, or ad/post about 'post once publish everywhere'
journey_stages.channel: Social media, creator referral, organic search

journey_stages.trigger: Visits landing page, sees free tier, compares to Linktree + Gumroad + Discord stack
Signs up free, connects first social account, creates first post
Posts regularly, starts community, lists first product
First sale or first paid community member
Upgrades to Pro, connects more platforms, builds course

user_types.label: Established Creator
user_types.description: Growing team, monetizing, scaling. Has existing revenue streams and audience. Evaluates CreatorOS as consolidation — replace 5 tools with 1. Cares about reliability, analytics depth, and time saved.
goals: Consolidate distribution into one tool and eliminate manual cross-posting
Scale course and product sales without adding more platforms
Get unified analytics across all platforms in one dashboard
Automate repetitive tasks — welcome sequences, DM responses, email funnels
Manage a small team with proper permissions
pain_points: Paying $300-500/month across 6-8 SaaS tools that do not talk to each other
No single view of total revenue, audience size, or content performance
Team members need access to posting but not billing — no granular permissions anywhere
Switching between tools for different tasks wastes hours per week
Content scheduling across platforms requires manual calendar management

journey_stages.trigger: Peer recommendation, creator community discussion, or pain-point search
journey_stages.channel: Word of mouth, creator communities, SEO

journey_stages.trigger: Requests demo or trial, compares feature matrix against current stack
journey_stages.channel: Pro trial, feature comparison page, onboarding call

journey_stages.trigger: Imports existing content, connects all social accounts, migrates community
journey_stages.channel: Import tools, connected accounts setup, migration wizard

journey_stages.trigger: Runs full workflow through CreatorOS — post, distribute, sell, analyze
Invites team members, sets roles and permissions
Recommends CreatorOS to peers, becomes case study

user_types.label: Creator Business
user_types.description: Team or agency operating a creator brand as a business. Diversified revenue. Needs API access, white-label, enterprise analytics, and team management. Evaluates on scale, reliability, and customization.
goals: Run entire creator business from one platform with API access for custom integrations
White-label the storefront and community under their own brand
Enterprise-grade analytics with export, custom reports, and cross-platform attribution
Multi-seat team management with granular permissions per function
Reduce transaction fees to maximize margin at scale
pain_points: Current tools cap out at scale — rate limits, feature ceilings, no API
White-labeling requires custom development on top of existing platforms
Finance team needs data exports that creator tools do not provide
Managing 10+ team members across 5 tools with separate logins and permission models
Transaction fees at volume represent significant revenue leakage

journey_stages.trigger: Manager or ops lead evaluates platforms for consolidation project
Evaluates API, white-label capabilities, migration feasibility
journey_stages.channel: API docs, sandbox environment, sales engineer

journey_stages.trigger: Custom pricing, SLA discussion, feature commitments
Phased migration of content, products, community, and team
Full production use across team with custom integrations
Adds more brands, sub-accounts, or higher tier features

user_types.label: Consumer — Superfan
user_types.description: Follows multiple creators actively, high engagement. Wants a single feed to track all their favorite creators across platforms. Comments, shares, and purchases frequently. Values community belonging.
goals: See all content from followed creators in one feed without visiting 6 apps
Get notified when favorite creators post, go live, or release products
Save and organize content across creators for later consumption
Engage in creator communities alongside other fans
pain_points: Missing posts because platform algorithms suppress content
Following creators on 4 platforms means 4 separate feeds with no cross-view
Notifications are scattered across apps and easy to miss
Community access requires separate Discord servers for each creator

journey_stages.trigger: Creator they follow shares CreatorOS link, or they find marketplace/community
Creates consumer account to follow creator or join community
Follows multiple creators, joins communities, saves content
Buys a digital product, course, or community membership
Daily feed check, community participation, course progress

user_types.label: Consumer — Learner
user_types.description: Course purchaser and skill seeker. Primary interaction is course consumption, not social feed. Values progress tracking, structured learning, and certificates. Less interested in community unless it supports learning.
goals: Find high-quality courses from creators they trust
Track progress across multiple courses with clear completion milestones
Get certificates or proof of completion for professional development
Ask questions and get help within the course community
pain_points: Course platforms are separate from the creator's other content — missed context
No unified view of all courses purchased across different creators
Progress resets or gets lost when switching devices
Certificate quality varies — some platforms offer nothing

journey_stages.trigger: Searches for course by topic, or creator promotes course
journey_stages.channel: Marketplace search, creator profile, social promotion

journey_stages.trigger: Reviews course curriculum, preview content, ratings, price
Buys course (one-time or subscription)
Works through modules, watches videos, completes quizzes
Finishes course, receives certificate
Enrolls in next course from same or different creator

user_types.label: Consumer — Community Member
user_types.description: Joins communities for belonging, networking, and niche conversation. Less interested in purchasing products — more in connecting with like-minded people around a creator's topic. Overlaps with Discord users.
goals: Find communities around topics they care about
Connect with like-minded people and build relationships
Participate in discussions without the noise of public social media
Access exclusive content or channels within the community
pain_points: Discord servers are hard to discover and have steep onboarding
Communities across creators are fragmented — separate servers, logins, notification settings
Free communities lack quality control; paid ones are scattered across platforms
No unified profile across communities — reputation does not transfer

journey_stages.trigger: Creator invites them, or they browse community directory
journey_stages.channel: Creator promotion, community directory, invite link

journey_stages.trigger: Joins free community or purchases membership for paid community
Reads channels, absorbs culture, finds their footing
Posts first message, responds to others, contributes
Becomes regular, recognized by community, helps newcomers
Joins more communities, purchases creator's other products

user_types.label: UGC Creator
user_types.description: Creates content on behalf of brands in response to campaign briefs. Not building their own audience — making content for others. Paid per deliverable. Overlaps with Emerging Creator tier but motivated by brand campaign income.
goals: Find well-paying UGC campaign briefs that match their niche and style
Apply to campaigns quickly with a strong portfolio
Submit deliverables efficiently and get paid fast
Build a reputation and track record that unlocks better campaigns
pain_points: UGC campaign discovery is fragmented across many platforms and DMs
Payment terms vary wildly and payment is often delayed
No centralized portfolio or reputation score across campaigns
Brief requirements are unclear, leading to revision cycles

journey_stages.trigger: Hears about CreatorOS UGC marketplace, creates profile with portfolio
Browses available campaign briefs, filters by niche/pay/requirements
Applies to campaign with pitch and portfolio samples
Accepted by brand, receives brief, creates content
journey_stages.channel: Campaign workspace, brief viewer, editing studio

journey_stages.trigger: Uploads deliverable for brand review
Brand approves, payment processed
Completes campaigns, builds rating, gets invited to premium campaigns

user_types.label: Advertiser
user_types.description: Business or brand running paid campaigns on the CreatorOS ads platform. Targets creator audiences with sponsored content. Also may run UGC campaigns. Evaluates based on audience quality, targeting precision, and ROAS.
goals: Reach creator audiences with precise targeting by niche, demographics, and engagement
Run UGC campaigns to get authentic brand content at scale
Measure campaign performance with clear attribution and ROAS metrics
Manage budget efficiently with bid optimization and spend controls
pain_points: Creator audiences are walled inside platform ecosystems with limited targeting
UGC procurement is manual — emailing creators, negotiating rates, managing deliverables
Attribution across creator channels is nearly impossible
Minimum spends on major platforms price out smaller advertisers

journey_stages.trigger: Evaluates CreatorOS ads platform for audience reach and targeting capabilities
journey_stages.channel: Ads landing page, case studies, sales outreach

journey_stages.trigger: Creates advertiser account, sets up billing, connects payment method
Creates first campaign with targeting, budget, creative, and schedule
Reviews performance, adjusts targeting/bids, tests creative variants
Increases budget on winning campaigns, adds UGC campaigns
Becomes recurring advertiser with monthly/quarterly budget allocation

creator_onboarding.description: Creator onboarding flow — from signup through first value moment (first published post)
creator_onboarding.design_principle: Every step must deliver visible value. No empty states. Prefill aggressively. Default to working, not configuring.

steps.name: signup
steps.action: Create account with email or social OAuth
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — Passport.js exists but is broken (comparePasswords returns true for all). Target: Clerk.

steps.name: profile_setup
steps.action: Set display name, bio, profile image. Import from existing social account if connected.
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — profile editing exists on profile.tsx but no dedicated onboarding screen

steps.name: connect_platforms
steps.action: Connect social accounts (Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitch, Pinterest). At least 1 required for cross-posting value. Skip-able.
steps.implementation_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED — no connected accounts management, no OAuth flows for social platforms
steps.decision_point: Skip or connect. Skipping delays core value proposition (cross-posting) but allows exploration.

steps.name: choose_focus
steps.action: Select primary creator category (content creator, educator, community builder, commerce seller, multi-mode). This personalizes the dashboard and feature emphasis.
steps.decision_point: Determines which modules surface first in the dashboard. Content creator sees feed first. Educator sees course builder first. Commerce seller sees marketplace first.

steps.name: first_post
steps.action: Create and publish first post. This is the activation moment — creator sees their content go live. If platforms were connected, they see cross-posting in action.
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — create-post.tsx exists with text/photo/video/audio support. No cross-platform distribution.

steps.name: dashboard_tour
steps.action: Guided tour highlighting key areas: feed, communities, marketplace, analytics. Dismissible. Surfaces contextual tips as creator explores.
steps.implementation_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED — no guided tour or tooltip system

creator_onboarding.activation_metric: First post published (with or without cross-platform distribution)
implementation_gaps: No dedicated onboarding screens — profile setup is only on profile.tsx edit mode
No connected accounts / OAuth for social platforms
No creator category selection or personalization
No guided tour or progressive disclosure system

consumer_onboarding.description: Consumer onboarding flow — from discovery through first meaningful engagement
consumer_onboarding.design_principle: Consumers arrive through creator links. Show them what they came for immediately. Sign-up wall only for actions that require identity (follow, join, purchase).

steps.name: landing
steps.action: Consumer arrives via creator link. Sees creator content, product, or community before any sign-up. Browsing is gated-free.
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — profile.tsx exists but no public-facing unauthenticated view. Auth is required for all routes.
steps.first_experience: Content-first. The consumer sees what they came for. No sign-up wall on browse.

steps.name: signup_trigger
steps.action: Prompted to create account when they try to follow, join community, purchase, or save content. Minimal friction — email + password or social OAuth.
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — auth-page.tsx exists but auth is broken. No social OAuth.
steps.first_experience: Sign-up appears contextual to action, not as a gate to browsing.

steps.name: interest_selection
steps.action: Select topics and creators of interest. Populates initial feed with relevant content instead of empty state.
steps.first_experience: Consumer immediately gets a personalized feed based on selections.

steps.name: first_engagement
steps.action: Consumer lands on personalized feed. Can follow creators, browse communities, and explore marketplace.
steps.implementation_status: PARTIAL — explore.tsx exists with posts and stories. No personalization algorithm. No 'For You' vs 'Following' toggle.
steps.first_experience: Feed populated with content from selected interests and followed creator.

consumer_onboarding.activation_metric: First follow, first community join, or first purchase — whichever happens first
implementation_gaps: No unauthenticated browsing — all routes require login currently
No consumer-specific onboarding (interest selection, personalized feed)
No social OAuth for faster consumer signup
No 'For You' algorithm or personalized feed
Auth is broken (same Passport.js vulnerability affects consumer flow)

journeys.goal: Create and publish first piece of content

steps.action: Creator lands on feed after onboarding. Sees example content and CTA to create first post.
steps.outcome: Creator clicks create button (FloatingActionButton or top nav)

steps.action: Creator selects media type (text, photo, video, audio, voice). Composes content. Adds tags, location, poll if desired.
Creator selects target platforms. If no platforms connected, publishes to CreatorOS native only. If connected, selects which platforms to cross-post to.
Creator hits publish. Content goes live on CreatorOS and selected platforms.
steps.outcome: Post is live. Creator sees confirmation with links to each platform.

steps.action: Creator sees their post in the feed. Views, likes, and comments begin accumulating.
steps.outcome: Creator experiences first value — content is distributed.

journeys.happy_path: Creator has connected at least one social platform during onboarding. First post is cross-posted. Creator sees content appear on both CreatorOS feed and connected platform. Analytics begin populating within minutes.
edge_cases: No platforms connected — post publishes to CreatorOS native only. Value prop is reduced to local feed visibility only.
Large media upload on slow connection — needs progress indicator and retry on failure. No upload progress UI exists currently.
Creator abandons mid-composition — draft auto-save needed. No draft system exists currently.
First post gets zero engagement — need seeded discovery mechanism to prevent empty-feed discouragement.

implemented: Post creation with multiple media types

journeys.goal: Create a branded community with channels and membership tiers

steps.action: Creator navigates to communities section. Sees existing communities and CTA to create new one.
Creator names community, writes description, sets icon color, chooses visibility (public/private).
Creator creates channels (general, announcements, off-topic, etc.). Sets channel types (text, voice, video). Configures which channels are free vs paid-tier only.
Creator sets up membership tiers: free (basic channels), paid monthly (premium channels, DMs with creator, exclusive content).
Creator generates invite link, shares on social platforms. Configures auto-post announcing community launch.
Members join. Creator and members interact in channels. Pinned messages, reactions, threads.

journeys.happy_path: Creator creates community, sets up 3-5 channels with a free and paid tier, shares invite link on their platforms. First 50 members join within a week. Paid tier converts 5-10% of free members.
edge_cases: Community gets no members — creator needs discovery boost (marketplace listing, cross-promotion)
Spam/moderation issues — no moderation tools exist currently
Paid tier setup without Stripe — cannot collect payments currently
Voice/video channels — not implemented, text-only currently
Community ownership ambiguity — communities table has no creator FK currently

missing: Community ownership (no userId FK on communities table)

journeys.goal: Build and sell an online course with structured curriculum

steps.action: Creator opens course builder. Enters title, description, category, cover image.
Creator builds curriculum: creates modules (sections), adds lessons within modules. Each lesson can be video, text, quiz, or assignment. Drag-and-drop reordering.
Creator records or uploads video for each lesson. Adds supplementary text, downloadable resources. Sets drip schedule if applicable.
Creator sets price (one-time or subscription). Configures launch discount, bundle options, free preview lessons.
steps.outcome: Course is priced and configured for sale

steps.action: Creator previews course landing page. Reviews curriculum. Publishes to marketplace.
Creator monitors enrollment, completion rates, revenue, student feedback.
steps.outcome: Creator has data to improve course and marketing

journeys.happy_path: Creator builds a 5-module course with 20 lessons. Sets one-time price of $99. Publishes and promotes to their audience. Gets 50 enrollments in the first week. 60% completion rate.
edge_cases: Large video uploads — need chunked upload, progress tracking, and resume on failure
Creator abandons mid-build — course drafts must persist and be resumable
Student refund requests — need refund workflow integrated with payment
Quiz grading — need automatic grading for multiple-choice, manual review for assignments
Course updates after students enrolled — need versioning or notification system

missing: Entire course platform — no schema tables (courses, modules, lessons, enrollments), no UI pages, no video hosting, no progress tracking, no quiz system, no certificate generation

journeys.goal: List a digital product on the marketplace and complete first sale

steps.action: Creator opens product creation form. Enters title, description, price, category. Uploads product image.
Creator previews how the product appears in marketplace. Checks description, image, price display.
Product appears in marketplace listings. Consumers can browse, filter, and discover it.
Consumer views product detail page. Reads description, sees price, reviews. Clicks purchase.
Consumer enters payment information. Completes purchase via Stripe.
Creator sees sale reflected in revenue dashboard. Payout scheduled.

journeys.happy_path: Creator lists a $19 digital download (ebook/template). Shares link on social platforms. Consumer finds it via marketplace or direct link. Purchases. Creator gets payout minus transaction fee (8% on free tier = $1.52 fee, $17.48 to creator).
edge_cases: Consumer wants refund — no refund workflow exists
Digital delivery failure — no file hosting or delivery mechanism exists currently
Product has no reviews/ratings — cold start problem for trust
Creator changes price after consumer added to cart — race condition
High-value product ($500+) — consumer may want installment payments

implemented: Product creation form (title, description, price, category, image)
missing: Product reviews/ratings (schema field exists but no UI)

journeys.goal: Launch a UGC campaign, receive creator-made content, and pay creators

steps.action: Advertiser creates campaign: brand name, brief description, content requirements (format, length, style), budget per deliverable, total budget, deadline.
Campaign appears in UGC marketplace. UGC creators browse available campaigns by niche, pay, and requirements.
steps.outcome: Campaign is discoverable by UGC creators

steps.action: UGC creators apply with pitch and portfolio. Advertiser reviews applications, accepts or rejects.
Accepted creators produce content according to brief. Submit deliverables through the platform.
Advertiser reviews submitted content. Approves, requests revisions, or rejects. Approved content triggers payment.
steps.outcome: Content approved and ready to use

steps.action: Platform processes payment to approved creators. Advertiser sees total spend and content library.
steps.outcome: Creators paid, advertiser has content assets

journeys.happy_path: Brand creates a $5,000 UGC campaign for 10 videos at $500 each. 30 creators apply. Brand selects 10. All deliver within deadline. Brand approves 8 on first submission, 2 after one revision. All creators paid within 7 days.
edge_cases: Creator misses deadline — need grace period and replacement mechanism
Deliverable does not meet brief — revision workflow with clear limits (max 2 revisions)
Dispute over quality — need mediation/escalation path
Brand cancels mid-campaign — need partial payment policy for work already submitted
Creator submits copyrighted content — need content verification and rights assignment

missing: Entire UGC campaign system — no schema tables, no UI pages, no campaign workflow, no payment processing, no deliverable management

journeys.goal: Discover new creators and content through the feed and marketplace

steps.action: Consumer opens the explore feed. Sees content from followed creators and algorithmically suggested content.
Consumer taps through stories from creators they follow. Discovers new creators via story suggestions.
Consumer visits a new creator's profile. Sees their posts, products, community, and bio.
Consumer follows the creator. Creator's content now appears in their feed.
Consumer browses marketplace. Discovers products, courses, and communities from creators they follow and new creators.
Consumer saves content and products for later. Bookmarks serve as a personal library.
steps.outcome: Consumer organizes content for future engagement

journeys.happy_path: Consumer opens feed, sees post from followed creator, discovers tagged creator, visits their profile, follows them, browses their products in marketplace, saves a course for later purchase.
edge_cases: Cold start — new consumer with no follows sees empty feed. Need trending/suggested content.
Algorithm shows irrelevant content — need feedback mechanism (not interested, hide)
Creator posts are infrequent — feed feels empty. Need cross-platform aggregation.
Consumer follows 200+ creators — feed becomes overwhelming. Need algorithmic ranking.

journeys.goal: Find, purchase, and consume a course from a creator

steps.action: Consumer searches marketplace for courses by topic. Filters by price, rating, category.
Consumer views course landing page: curriculum outline, preview lessons, instructor bio, reviews, price.
Consumer enters payment. Completes purchase. Receives instant access.
Consumer works through course modules. Watches videos, reads text, takes quizzes. Progress auto-tracked.
Consumer completes all modules. Receives certificate. Course marked complete in profile.
Consumer visits creator's profile to see other courses and products. May leave a review on completed course.
steps.outcome: Consumer may purchase again or follow for future content

journeys.happy_path: Consumer searches for 'photography basics', finds a $49 course with 4.8 rating and 200 reviews. Purchases. Completes 12 lessons over 2 weeks. Receives certificate. Enrolls in the creator's advanced course.
edge_cases: Consumer wants to preview before buying — need free preview lessons
Consumer stops mid-course and returns weeks later — need resume exactly where they left off
Course content is updated after purchase — consumer needs notification and access to updated content
Consumer wants refund after starting — need refund policy tied to progress percentage
Course has community component — need gated community access tied to enrollment

missing: Entire course system — marketplace search/filter, course detail page, checkout, course player, progress tracking, quizzes, certificates, reviews. No schema tables exist for courses.

open_questions.question: Should consumer onboarding be completely gate-free (browse without account) or require signup before any interaction?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether unauthenticated routes exist, which affects SEO, sharing, and conversion funnel design.
options: Gate-free browsing with signup on action (follow/purchase/join)
Signup required but minimal (email only, complete profile later)
Fully gated (signup before seeing any content)
open_questions.recommendation: Gate-free browsing with signup on action — maximizes top-of-funnel while maintaining clear conversion points

open_questions.question: Should creator onboarding branch based on tier (emerging vs established) or be uniform with post-onboarding personalization?
open_questions.impact: Branched onboarding is more relevant per user but adds maintenance burden. Uniform onboarding is simpler but may feel generic.
options: Uniform onboarding with post-onboarding personalization based on stated goals
Adaptive onboarding that adjusts dynamically based on connected account metrics (follower count)
open_questions.recommendation: Adaptive onboarding — connect accounts first, infer tier from follower count, personalize remaining steps automatically

open_questions.question: What is the first monetization journey to implement — product sales (marketplace), course sales, or community memberships?
open_questions.impact: Determines which Stripe integration to build first and which schema tables to add first.
options: Digital product sales (simplest — single payment, file delivery)
Community memberships (recurring revenue, existing community UI)
Course sales (highest ticket, but course platform is fully missing)
open_questions.recommendation: Digital product sales first — lowest implementation effort (products table exists), clear transaction flow, proves payment infrastructure that all other types reuse

open_questions.question: Should UGC creators be a separate user type with distinct onboarding, or a mode/role within the existing creator type?
open_questions.impact: Separate type means distinct onboarding and profile. Role-based means shared profile with UGC capabilities toggled on.
options: Separate user type with distinct onboarding and profile
Role/mode within creator type — toggle UGC mode in settings
Hybrid — same account, separate UGC portfolio page
open_questions.recommendation: Hybrid — same creator account with a UGC portfolio tab. Reduces onboarding friction and lets emerging creators do both.

implementation_debt.description: Summary of implementation gaps between desired journeys and current codebase state

critical_blockers.description: Authentication is broken — comparePasswords returns true for all. No journey can be safely tested until auth works.
Zero payment infrastructure — no Stripe, no checkout, no orders table, no transaction processing.
critical_blockers.resolution: Implement Stripe Connect with marketplace pattern (platform collects, pays out to creators)

critical_blockers.description: No cross-platform distribution — the core product promise ('post once, publish everywhere') is unimplemented.
critical_blockers.resolution: Build connected accounts OAuth + platform API adapters for Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Twitter/X minimum

high_priority_gaps.description: No dedicated onboarding flow — new users land on explore page with no guidance.
high_priority_gaps.resolution: Build onboarding screen sequence: profile setup, platform connections, focus selection, first action

high_priority_gaps.description: Entire course platform is missing — no schema, no UI, no builder, no player.
high_priority_gaps.resolution: Design and build courses, modules, lessons, enrollments tables + course builder UI + course player

high_priority_gaps.description: No search functionality anywhere in the app.
high_priority_gaps.resolution: Implement full-text search across posts, products, creators, communities

high_priority_gaps.description: No content or audience analytics — only a basic revenue chart.
high_priority_gaps.resolution: Build analytics dashboard with content performance, audience growth, engagement metrics

medium_priority_gaps.description: No feed algorithm — all content is chronological with no personalization or For You/Following toggle.
Entire UGC campaign system is missing.
Communities table has no creator FK — ownership is ambiguous.
All routes require authentication — no unauthenticated browsing for consumers.
